output.methodChoice: Collected X8 (independent dryer and throat moisture measurements, incl. same-lot PD-1 vs D5 trial) and X3 (MES rejects by press, supplier, shift, operator group). Stopped at 2 items.

answers.reasoning: Arnholt run on Press 7 runs at 0.8% rejects, and Arnholt dried in a -40 C portable dryer gives 0.8%. Arnholt is not defective by itself.

answers.evidence_note: Quillan resin through D5 gives 0.9% rejects, normal.

output.brief: The rejects come from the combination of Arnholt resin and the degraded D5 dryer. Arnholt resin dried in D5 runs at about 10% rejects, while Arnholt dried in a properly working dryer (D7 or portable PD-1) runs at about 0.8%, and Quillan through D5 stays at 0.9%. The same Arnholt lot went from 10.4% in D5 to 0.8% in PD-1 the next day. The six new operators are not the cause: experienced operators on the same Arnholt material reject at the same rate as the new hires. Dropping Arnholt or disciplining the operators would not fix this. I am fairly confident in the dryer-plus-resin finding. One caveat: all Arnholt samples came from the north annex, so storage conditions could be part of the moisture problem. This is not yet tested. This week: repair D5's heater and desiccant, restore its original alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until it reads -40 C. Add a moisture check on each resin lot. Do not put the operators on improvement plans.
